title: Spike: rapid coverage roulette and effort estimator
content:
Purpose:
One-off estimator to quickly surface who to ping and how much effort is likely needed for small surge/blitz coverage (2–72h). Useful for rotation leads, on-call handoffs, and ad-hoc coverage asks during launches. Not exhaustive — treat as an operational aide for fast decisions.

How to use:
- Fill in row with scope, owner, ETA window, rough effort (low/med/high and hour estimate), and whether a handoff or page is required.
- Use Criticality to decide immediate paging vs. async.
- Row Notes should capture blockers, required approvals, and known downstream impacts.

Quick table (rows are intentionally terse — this is a working scratchpad):

Columns: Item | Proposed owner | ETA window | Effort (hrs est) | Effort bucket | Criticality (P0/P1/P2) | Hand-off needed? (y/n) | Primary blockers / quick notes

1. Fallback routing smoke test | Jonah Patel | 2–4h | 3 | low | P0 | y | needs access to test cluster; add runbook link; prod-key required
2. Regional burst capacity check (EU-west) | Maya Ortiz | 4–8h | 6 | med | P1 | y | quota lookup + partner-SPOC; may need Dedicated uplift request
3. Customer B onboarding run (pilot) | Luca Romano | 6–24h | 5 | med | P1 | n | pre-auth tokens needed; schedule with CS; regression checklist attached
4. Quick KV-cache eviction script + validation | Priya Nair | 1–2h | 2 | low | P0 | y | small blast radius; rollback path noted in notes; 1 engineer OK
5. Latency sample sweep for route X | Eng rotation | 8–12h | 8 | high | P1 | n | sampling script in ops repo; watch for noise from canary
6. Billing tally check for ad-hoc burst | Finance contact | 12–36h | 4 | low | P2 | n | requires billing export; might be delayed by 24h
7. Short-lived model fallback test (quantized variant) | Applied ML | 3–6h | 6 | med | P1 | y | model artifact staging; quant profile needs sign-off
8. Integrations sanity for vendor Y | Solutions Eng | 2–6h | 3 | low | P2 | n | vendor rate-limits unknown; include integration owner on loop
9. Oncall rotation swap and coverage note | SRE lead | 0.5–1h | 1 | low | P0 | y | update calendar and incident routing; confirm backup oncall
10. Minimal user communications draft (incidents/emergency) | Comms | 3–8h | 2 | low | P1 | n | templated copy available; legal review if data-exposure

Table totals (very approximate):
- Sum of effort (simple sum of est hrs): 40 hrs
- Median effort per task: 3.5 hrs
- Tasks flagged P0/P1 (immediate attention): rows 1,4,5,7,9,10 -> 6 tasks

Open questions / decision points (to capture quickly on the sheet):
- Who authorizes cross-regional uplift above reserved Dedicated? (stakeholder to note)
- Which partner contacts are active after hours for EU vendor Y? (Ops to confirm)
- Do we need a formal SLA exception to proceed for the pilot? (Legal/Trust check)

Suggested quick actions (for rotation lead):
- Triage P0 items first: allocate 1 engineer each and page owners.
- If total estimated load > 12h in next 12h window, call for surge assist (email to "rotation-surge@redwood.com").
- Track actual vs estimated hours in adjacent column 'actual_hrs' and capture variance after task closes.

Notes to self (rough):
- This sheet is intentionally lightweight — copy into more formal tracker if the scope grows beyond a day.
- Keep a column for 'followup-ticket' to attach any created Jira/Linear IDs.
- We should consider automating the ETA buckets from on-call calendar in a later iteration.
